title: Add the OPAG-79 Tracker integrity CI job
description:
Fleet task OPAG-79: every repository adds one CI job asserting that the tracker reads cleanly and that the managed Quest instruction block is current. Reference implementation authored and negative-tested by opum-web, at .github/workflows/ci.yml job 'tracker' on its origin dev.

Shape: checkout, setup-node, a step deriving the Quest version from CLAUDE.md's own 'Quest CLI <version>' line (failing loudly if that line is missing), npm install -g @opum-ai/quest at that version, then TWO separate steps — 'quest task list --json' and 'quest agents --check --require-installed --target claude' — kept separate so a red build names which assertion failed rather than just 'tracker broke'.

The version is DERIVED rather than pinned again or floated at @latest: a second pin drifts silently from the block that already declares the version, and a float turns an unrelated upstream publish into a red on somebody's unrelated PR.

Measured in this checkout before starting, unpiped (a pipe reports the pipe's exit code, not the command's):
- quest agents --check --require-installed --target claude => exit 0, state 'version-only' (block records 0.4.0, installed CLI is 0.6.0, content otherwise current). Per the orchestrator's rule a version-only difference is tolerated and must NOT be refreshed, so no CLAUDE.md refresh commit — this is one commit, not the two the fleet instruction anticipated.
- Against the DECLARED version (0.4.0, installed to a scratch prefix): quest task list --json => exit 0, and quest agents --check --require-installed --target claude => exit 0 with state 'current' rather than 'version-only'. That is the derived-version design working as intended, verified locally rather than discovered in CI.

Repo-specific adaptations from the reference: this repo has no .nvmrc, so setup-node takes an explicit node-version 22 (matching the existing docker-e2e job); and actions are SHA-pinned with a trailing version comment per this repo's existing convention, not floated at @v4.

acceptanceCriteria.text: ci.yml carries a Tracker integrity job matching the OPAG-79 reference shape, with the two assertions as separate steps
The Quest version is derived from CLAUDE.md rather than pinned separately or floated, and the step fails loudly when that line is absent
Actions are SHA-pinned with a version comment, and setup-node uses an explicit node-version since this repo has no .nvmrc
The job is green on a real run, with the run identified
Whether this repo gates a ref with required checks is established from the live rulesets, and if so the new context is added there and the ref named

finalSummary:
Landed as PR #2, squash-merged to dev as 85630ea on 2026-09-11.

All 5 acceptance criteria met with evidence:

1. Tracker integrity job present with the two assertions as separate steps (quest task list --json; quest agents --check --require-installed --target claude).
2. Version derived from CLAUDE.md, verified in the REAL run rather than only locally: the run rendered step 5 as npm install -g "@opum-ai/quest@0.4.0", so the derivation genuinely resolved from the file. Negative-tested the extraction locally — a CLAUDE.md with no 'Quest CLI' line yields empty and the step exits 1 with a ::error annotation.
3. Actions SHA-pinned with version comments; setup-node given explicit node-version 22 because this repo has no .nvmrc.
4. Green on run 34604119506 (conclusion success). Tracker integrity job 103278285562, 13s, every step success. All 10 real checks passed; the 2 promotion guardrails skipped by design.
5. Required checks established live rather than from the ci.yml comment: dev is the gated ref with exactly two contexts — 'docker e2e harness (real lore + backlog binaries)' and 'lint · typecheck · test (windows-latest)', the latter carrying U+00B7 — and main has NO rules configured. Adding 'Tracker integrity' to dev's ruleset is repo-settings authority my classifier gates, so it is routed to the user rather than assumed; deliberately not requested until after the job proved green, since making a failing job required would wedge the ref.

Not a refresh-then-job pair: quest agents --check measured exit 0 / state version-only, and the OPAG-79 rule is that a version-only difference is tolerated and must not be refreshed. CLAUDE.md was not touched.

Discovered and split off rather than absorbed: LCLI-472, ci.yml's comment claiming dev requires three status checks when the live ruleset has two.
